The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS) and the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) seek an outstanding candidate to fill a tenure track Fellow (Assistant Professor level) position in the field of Computational Biology. The candidate is expected to start autumn 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

We are looking for a researcher with clear potential for research excellence who thrives in and is inspired by interdisciplinary collaboration. The ideal candidate will be expected to contribute to high-quality research in their field while embracing DIAS’s mission of curiosity-driven inquiry and interdisciplinary dialogue. The successful candidate should have a strong and promising research profile, with potential for attracting external research funding, and a demonstrated ability to work across disciplines. The candidate will be attached to both the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology and DIAS and should be prepared to engage in multiple and diverse research environments at SDU. Teaching obligations will be reduced compared to a standard assistant professorship at SDU, allowing more time for research and leadership activities.

Who are we looking for a highly competitive and collaborative assistant professor in the field of Computational Biology.

We seek a researcher with expertise in the field of Computational Biology, who is eager to develop their research career within the DIAS framework. The ideal candidate should demonstrate: 

• 
Excellence in the ability to formulate, drive and publish scientific work in the field of Computational Biology. 

• 
Future ambitious research program that synergizes and complements those of existing groups in the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology.

• 
A commitment to engaging in boundary-crossing interdisciplinary research and dialogue.

• 
A strong commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration, contributing to research that bridges multiple fields. 

• 
Strong interest in driving internationally competitive research activities at the highest level of ambition. 

• 
Engagement in various forms of research dissemination, including interdisciplinary research and dialogue. 

Qualifications

Successful applicants must: 

• 
Hold a PhD or similar qualifications within relevant fields of Computational Biology. To qualify for the position as Assistant Professor you must have obtained a PhD or similar degree by the application deadline and typically have demonstrated min. 2 years of successful postdoctoral research. 

• 
Exhibit curiosity-driven research excellence, thinking beyond traditional boundaries. 

• 
Be fluent in English.

• 
Show potential for attracting external research funding. Experience in applying for external funding and a strong international network are considered comparative advantages.

• 
Have research publications that demonstrate excellence and broad thinking. 

The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS)

DIAS at SDU is a hub for interdisciplinary excellence at and beyond the frontier of knowledge, bringing together outstanding researchers from various disciplines to foster groundbreaking interdisciplinary research and bold innovation. DIAS nurtures a collaborative and curiosity-driven environment, encouraging scholars to think outside the box and challenge conventional boundaries. The institute values open-minded exploration and an ambitious yet collegial atmosphere with a strong sense of community. Researchers affiliated with DIAS are expected to contribute actively to DIAS activities, and engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across faculties and departments, both nationally and internationally. 

The Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (BMB)

The Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology at the University of Southern Denmark is an international research environment with more than 200 employees working across biochemistry, molecular biology, biomedicine, bioinformatics, and related disciplines. Our research addresses fundamental mechanisms of life and disease, increasingly through advanced technologies, integrated omics approaches, and computational analysis of complex biological data.

BMB combines strong basic research with close links to healthcare, biotechnology, and industry, and places high value on interdisciplinary collaboration, innovation, and translation. We offer an open and ambitious working environment with researchers and students from more than 25 countries, where computational and experimental scientists work together to address biologically and medically important questions.

Additional information

For further information about being a fellow at DIAS, please contact DIAS director Sten Rynning at +45 6550 2193 or via email at director-dias@sdu.dk.

For more questions about the position please contact Head of the Department, Jakob Møller Jensen (jakobm@bmb.sdu.dk), or DIAS Chair Professor Susanne Mandrup (s.mandrup@bmb.sdu.dk).

Application, salary, and employment terms

The position is based at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology in Odense and includes regular participation in DIAS and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Employment is governed by the collective agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

The salary comprises a seniority-based base salary and a centrally agreed supplement.

Additional supplements may be negotiated locally.

As of 1 August 2026, the annual salary for an Assistant Professor is DKK 480,224.96 (salary level 6), consisting of a base salary of DKK 417,456 and a supplement of DKK 62,768.96.

All amounts are stated before tax, before added pension (18.07%), and any additional supplements. Pension contributions are paid by SDU, and both salary components (the annual salary and the supplement) are pensionable. For more details on salary and taxation, please refer to the provided links about salary and taxation.

Danish Tenure Track Programme

An appointment as Assistant Professor (Danish tenure track) is limited to a six-year term. The academic assessment for promotion to Associate Professor must be initiated no later than the end of the fifth year of employment. However, a tenure track assistant professor may request an earlier assessment within the first four years.

If the initial assessment is negative, one reassessment may be conducted during the final six months prior to a potential transition. A maximum of two assessments may be undertaken.

A positive assessment leads to appointment to a permanent Associate Professor position. If the final assessment is negative, the employment may be terminated in accordance with the applicable collective agreement.

A six-year development plan for the tenure track programme is established at the start of employment.

Application requirements

The application must include the following:

• 
Letter of motivation that clearly explains the applicant's interest, qualifications, and motivation for the position.

• 
Detailed CV including documentation of experience, and contacts for possible references. 

• 
An elaborated research and funding plan (max 4 pages) for the next three years including a description of synergy with the department's activities and the potential to benefit from DIAS’s interdisciplinary environment.

• 
Copies of certificates/Diplomas (Master and PhD degree).

• 
Complete list of publications, indicating which publications are most relevant for the position.

• 
List of max. 10 most important publications with a short summary and description of your contribution to the work (max two pages).

• 
Applicants are requested to submit a teaching portfolio with the application as documentation for teaching experience as well as supervision qualifications. Formal application instructions and a guide for the teaching portfolio can be found here.

All application materials must be submitted in English, and only applications written in English will be considered.

We recommend that international applicants take the time to visit websites of Work in Denmark and the International Staff Office at SDU. Here you can find information and facts about moving to, working and living in Denmark. 

Submission guidelines

• 
Files must be submitted in PDF format.

• 
If multiple files are needed for a single section, combine them into one PDF file.

• 
Zip files, image files (jpg, png, etc.), and password-protected PDF files will not be accepted. All PDF files must be unlocked to allow binding.

• 
Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

Assessment

Shortlisting may be used as part of the assessment process. Read about shortlisting at SDU.

Assessment of applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicant will receive the part of the evaluation that concerns them. 

Applications that are incomplete with regards to the above requirements will not be assessed by the committee. Shortlisting and tests may be used in the assessment process and references may be obtained. 

About SDU
SDU is committed to fostering a diverse staff that reflects society’s diversity. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background.
SDU was founded in 1966 and now has over 27,000 students, nearly 20% of whom are international. SDU employs more than 3,800 staff and offers 115 study programmes across disciplines such as the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, health sciences, and engineering. While SDU’s main campus is in Odense, it also has campuses in other locations.

Equal opportunity employment
The University of Southern Denmark is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, colour, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, or any other protected status.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes our staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, are subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position. 

How to apply
Applications must be submitted electronically via the "Apply online" link provided in the job posting.

If you experience technical problems, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk.

D’ANGLETERRE IS SEARCHING FOR A FULL-TIME DOORMAN

At d’Angleterre, the guest experience begins before a guest even steps inside the hotel.

We are looking for a warm, confident and attentive Doorman to join our Front Office team. As one of the first people our guests meet and one of the last they see when they leave, you play an important role in creating the lasting impression they take with them.

This role is about much more than opening doors. You represent d’Angleterre through genuine hospitality, personal recognition and an ability to anticipate what each guest may need.

ABOUT THE JOB

As our Doorman, you will create seamless and personalised arrival and departure experiences while ensuring the hotel entrance operates smoothly.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Welcoming hotel, restaurant and event guests with warmth and genuine personal attention

• Recognising returning guests and anticipating individual needs

• Opening hotel and car doors, assisting with luggage and guiding guests to their destination

• Parking and retrieving guest vehicles safely and handling keys with care

• Coordinating taxis, transfers and guest movement with Concierge, Reception and the luggage team

• Staying informed about arrivals, departures, VIP guests and inhouse events to help personalise the experience

• Sharing relevant guest preferences and requests with colleagues to ensure seamless service

• Providing knowledgeable information about the hotel and Copenhagen

• Maintaining a welcoming, polished and safe hotel entrance

• Taking ownership of guest requests and consistently representing the service and discretion expected at d’Angleterre

ABOUT YOU

You have a natural ability to make people feel welcome. You are warm and approachable while remaining polished, professional and attentive to detail.

Experience from a luxury hotel or another high-end guest-facing environment is preferred, but your personality and instinct for hospitality are just as important.

You remain calm in a busy environment, communicate confidently in English and enjoy working as part of a team. Danish and other languages are an advantage, as is a good knowledge of Copenhagen.

A valid driving licence suitable for driving guest vehicles in Denmark is required, and you must be comfortable parking different types of vehicles.

The position includes flexible shifts across days, afternoons and weekends.

WE OFFER

You will join one of Copenhagen’s most iconic luxury hotels and become part of an ambitious team dedicated to creating exceptional and personalised guest experiences.

As Doorman, you hold a particularly visible place within that experience.

You are not simply standing at the entrance to d’Angleterre. You are representing it.

ABOUT HOTEL D’ANGLETERRE

For more than 265 years, Hotel d’Angleterre has welcomed guests in the heart of Copenhagen. Today, we continue to combine our heritage with an ambition to develop and set new standards for luxury hospitality.

We believe exceptional service is ultimately about how we make people feel. And often, that experience begins with the person at the door.

Are you an inspiring and hands-on leader with a passion for luxury hospitality, impeccable standards and creating exceptional guest experiences?

You combine strong operational knowledge with warmth, structure and an exceptional eye for detail. You are comfortable making decisions, setting clear expectations and creating accountability, while leading with respect and genuine care for your team.

You have experience with team development, training, workforce planning, budgeting, labour productivity, inventory management and quality assurance. You communicate clearly, remain calm under pressure and enjoy working collaboratively across departments.

Most importantly, you understand that exceptional Housekeeping is not only about what a guest sees, but how the room and the experience make them feel.

Professional English is required, while Danish or other languages will be considered an advantage.

We offer

You will join one of Scandinavia's most iconic luxury hotels and take responsibility for a department that plays a defining role in the d’Angleterre experience.

Here, tradition and high standards go hand in hand with a genuine ambition to continuously evolve. You will have the opportunity to shape Housekeeping operations, develop people and processes, and contribute directly to the quality of the hotel and the experiences we create for our guests.

You will become part of an ambitious and professional environment where personalised service, development and mutual respect are at the heart of everything we do.

Rather than developing new medicines, we focus on finding smarter ways to bring existing treatments to patients, creating value for pharmacies, healthcare systems, and society.

We encourage people to ask questions, challenge assumptions, and take ownership. Across teams, functions, and markets, you will find a collaborative and supportive culture built on trust, respect, and a flat hierarchy where everyone has a voice and direct access to decision-makers.

When you join Orifarm, you will be empowered to make a real impact from day one. We offer autonomy and great opportunities for career advancement, giving you a valuable start to your career. As our student assistant, you may have the opportunity to complete an internship or collaborate with us on your bachelor’s or master’s thesis. We value flexibility and provide a hybrid work model with the possibility of working from home two days a week.

We invite you to join Orifarm, if you are curious, ambitious, and accept the challenge of making affordable healthcare accessible.

We encourage everyone to apply

At Orifarm, we welcome people from all backgrounds, recognizing that the best outcomes come from a diverse and inclusive work environment. Our commitment is to create an environment where different perspectives and skills drive innovation and contribute to a sustainable future. By creating such an environment, we are confident that we can achieve better results together.

Are you an experienced SMD Operator with a keen eye for quality, stable processes and precision-driven electronics manufacturing? Do you thrive in a technical environment where you take responsibility, work in a structured manner and actively contribute to a strong team? Then you could be our next experienced SMD Operator at NECAS A/S.

About the position
As an SMD Operator at NECAS, you will play a key role in the operation of our SMD lines – the heart of our electronics manufacturing. You will be responsible for setting up, monitoring and optimising processes, ensuring that production meets our high quality standards.
The electronics you help produce are used in everything from industrial and marine applications to defence and aerospace – industries where precision and reliability are essential.
You will become part of a highly skilled team and report to the Team Leader.

Your responsibilities
SMD line operation and preparation

• Operate and monitor SMD equipment, including solder paste printer, SPI, pick-and-place, AOI and reflow oven
• Prepare the line for production changeovers, including programmes, materials, feeder setup and documentation
• Ensure stable operation in accordance with production plans and work instructions
• Work with supporting processes such as the washing machine and stencil cleaner

Quality and inspection

• Carry out process and quality inspections, including visual inspection and First Article Inspection
• Analyse AOI results and respond to deviations
• Ensure the correct handling of materials and components, including batch control, traceability and shelf life
• Work in accordance with the IPC-A-610 standard (certification provided where required)
• Record defects and deviations in the quality management system

Collaboration and continuous improvement

• Ensure good communication and effective handovers between shifts
• Share knowledge and support colleagues in their daily work
• Contribute suggestions for improving processes and workflows
• Maintain order and structure in the SMD area in accordance with 5S principles

About you
We are looking for a candidate who already has solid experience in SMD production and is able to work independently in a technically demanding role.

We expect you to:

• Have a minimum of 3 years' experience with SMD equipment or electronics manufacturing
• Be structured and able to maintain an overview, even during busy periods
• Take responsibility and respond quickly when something deviates from the standard
• Be a team player who contributes positively to the team
• Have a technical understanding and an interest in working with advanced equipment
• Language: good command of English, spoken and written

What we offer
At NECAS, you will become part of a growing company where quality and professional expertise are at the heart of what we do. You will receive:

• A thorough introduction to our processes and equipment
• Opportunities for relevant training and certifications, such as IPC-A-610
• A strong team environment and an informal culture with a high level of professional expertise
• A workplace in Støvring's newest industrial area, close to the E45 motorway
• Competitive terms of employment, including pension and health insurance

About NECAS
NECAS is one of Denmark's leading EMS companies, manufacturing electronics for the industrial, marine/offshore, defence, aerospace and scientific sectors – industries where quality and precision are essential.
We are one of the few EMS manufacturers in Denmark with AS9100 certification for the aerospace industry. At NECAS, you will become part of a company experiencing significant growth, where you can develop your professional skills and help push the boundaries of Danish electronics manufacturing.

As we say: Built for trust.

How to apply
The position will be filled as soon as possible. We are inviting candidates to interviews on an ongoing basis, so please send your application and CV as soon as possible. We read all applications and will contact candidates we would like to get to know better.
If you have any questions, please contact Team Leader Mariana Surleac on +45 92 92 76 20.

jobs.description:
The Department of Sociology invites applications for a postdoctoral position in the research project FanVEX: Fanization of Violent Extremism on social media to commence by 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.
 
 The position is a full time fixed-term position for 30 months

  Introduction 
 Online fandom and violent extremism increasingly intersect on social media. Violent perpetrators may become objects of fandom, while extremist actors draw on fan practices and popular culture to circulate ideological messages and attract audiences (Warzel, 2025). As perpetrators and their admirers participate in digital communities and their practices overlap with mainstream fandom (Gartenstein-Ross et al., 2023; Davey & Ebner, 2017), established approaches to understanding radicalisation, motivations and the role of ideology face new challenges.

  FanVEX investigates how validation from fan communities may mobilise or accelerate violent action and which factors sustain participation in these communities. The project examines how fandom makes extremist content memetic and viral (Milner, 2016), combines ideology with popular culture (Driessen et al., 2025), and reproduces cultural scripts that can make violence appear conceivable, attractive or worthy of emulation. The aim is to advance theoretical and empirical understanding of these processes and generate insights relevant to prevention and threat assessment.

  FanVEX brings together researchers at the University of Copenhagen’s Department of Sociology (MOD-Lab: Microsociology of Online Deviance) and Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics (CODEX: Copenhagen Observatory of Digital Extremism), with international partners at Malmö University and Erasmus University Rotterdam. The postdoctoral researcher will be based at the Department of Sociology and will work in close collaboration with the wider FanVEX team. Professor Jakob Demant will be the main contact for the position.

  Duties and Responsibilities
 Typically, the primary focus of a postdoctoral position will be on research. However, a certain amount of teaching obligations may be required. Additional tasks beyond research and teaching may also be considered, but to a limited extent. The university will determine the final scope of the various responsibilities, and the emphasis may vary over time.

  The postdoctoral researcher will contribute particularly to Work Package 4 (WP4), which asks: How does engagement with popular culture contribute to the expression of extremist ideologies? WP4 examines whether references to popular culture function as humour, imitation, motivation, or legitimisation.

  WP4 combines data-driven analyses with digital ethnography. Its quantitative component uses co-occurrence network analysis to investigate how references to popular culture relate to ideological discourse, including material from 4chan imageboards such as /pol/ and /b/ (2021–2027). It also examines changes over time through burst-detection analysis. The qualitative component studies online communities, including incels.is and Stormfront, to understand how popular culture, fandom and anti-fan practices are incorporated into extremist environments. The analyses are designed to inform one another.
 
 The postdoctoral researcher will be expected to:
 
 - Contribute to the design, collection and analysis of digital data for WP4, with particular emphasis on quantitative network and text-based analyses.
 
 - Integrate data-driven findings with digital ethnographic insights and, where relevant, qualitative interviews.
 
 - Apply rigorous research ethics and data-protection procedures when working with sensitive online material.
 
 - Collaborate across disciplinary boundaries and contribute to project meetings and research activities.
 
 - Produce both collaboratively authored and individually authored scholarly publications during the appointment.

  Qualification Requirements 
 Applicants should hold a PhD in sociology, media studies, criminology, communication, digital humanities or a closely related discipline. We seek a researcher who can work productively across qualitative and quantitative approaches and contribute to interdisciplinary publications. In assessing applications, we will place particular emphasis on:

   	
• Experience with digital ethnography and qualitative interviewing. 	
• Competence in quantitative network analysis and data-driven analysis of digital content, such as co-occurrence, sentiment or temporal analyses. 	
• Knowledge of research ethics, data protection and the responsible handling of sensitive personal data. 	
• An interest in online extremism, participatory cultures, popular culture and/or digital deviance. 	
• Strong analytical writing skills and the ability to work collaboratively in an interdisciplinary team.   You can find further information about the qualification requirements for postdoctoral positions here: Bekendtgørelse om stillingsstruktur for videnskabeligt personale ved universiteter (in Danish only).

  You can also find further information about the postdoctoral position on our English webpage on career paths for early‑career researchers at the University of Copenhagen: Career at The University of Copenhagen.

  Strategy of the Faculty of the Social Sciences
 The Department of Sociology is part of the Faculty of the Social Sciences. The faculty is a successful academic community that strives to put knowledge into action by:

   	
• Engaging partners in the co-creation of knowledge, learning and social change. 	
• Empowering our students to become reflective and responsible citizens who have the vision, the knowledge and the competences to change society for the better. 	
• Energising global, European and Danish communities of knowledge by innovating research methodologies and by research findings with impact.   Assessment Criteria
 Applicants will primarily be assessed in relation to their research qualifications, including their publications, ability to conduct independent research and participate in research collaborations, and their experience of research management. In addition, the applicant’s research plan and research potential will be assessed in relation to the overall research project described above. 

  Teaching qualifications are not a requirement, but if the Postdoc is expected to teach, then documented teaching experience can be included in the overall assessment.  

  Application
 Please submit your application online. To apply, please click on the "Apply now" icon at the bottum of this page.
 The application must be written in English, and include the following attachments in PDF or Word format:

   	
• CV (max. 3 pages) 	
• Cover letter (max. 1 page) 	
• Documentation of qualifications (exam certificates and PhD diploma) 	
• Complete publication list (attached publications must be marked with an asterisk). The list must be structured systematically and divided into the following categories: 	
• Peer-reviewed publications: 	 		
• Monographs and anthologies 		
• Articles in journals 		
• Book chapters/anthology contributions, etc. 	 	 	
• Non-peer-reviewed publications: 	 		
• Publications disseminating research findings, etc. 	 	   You can attach a maximum of 3 publications. The publication dates must be clearly marked on the list. The selected publications must be uploaded as attachments and numbered 1-3. 

   	
• Research plan (max. 2 pages)   The plan should include a brief account of previous research, current research projects, and a forward-looking outline of the planned research contribution over the coming years. The plan should also describe your involvement in research organisation, research collaborations, and active participation in research environments at both local and international levels.

  Salary and Terms of Employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC).
 The salary range for postdoctoral positions starts at DKK /approximately EUR 39,900 (5,300 EUR) + an 18.07 % pension contribution. It is possible to negotiate salary supplements on an annual basis.

  Recruitment Process
 After the application deadline, the Head of Department will consider advice from the appointment committee and select applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether they have been shortlisted. The Head of Department will set up an expert assessment committee to assess the shortlisted applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. Each shortlisted applicant will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee's assessment before the appointment is announced.

  You can find further information on our recruitment process at: Recruitment process.

  International Applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about our services at: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen.

  An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of oppertunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity ect. To learn more about our diverse workplace and our participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in Research, please visit HR Excellence in Research – University of Copenhagen

jobs.occupation: PhD positions at the Cosmic Dawn Center
jobs.description:
The Cosmic Dawn Center (DAWN) at the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, invites applications for up to three PhD positions. The positions are part of a dedicated research project funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF).

  DAWN is a Center of Excellence funded by the Danish National Research Foundation (DNRF) and is located in the Copenhagen area at the Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), University of Copenhagen and the Space division of the Danish Technical University (DTU-Space). In addition, DAWN has several associates at major research institutes across Europe, North America, and Australia. DAWN brings together experts in all aspects of early Universe research and is deeply involved in major existing and upcoming surveys with JWST and HST (e.g. SPURS, COSMOS3D, FRESCO, COSMOS-Web, RUBIES, BEACON, and CLUTCH), ALMA (e.g. CHAMPS), and Euclid (e.g. Cosmic Dawn Survey of the deep fields), as well as simulations. 

   

  The projects

  Up to three PhD positions are available at DAWN/NBI. Two are as part of the DFF Sapere Aude-funded project “Revealing Massive Stars at Cosmic Dawn” in Associate Professor Charlotte Mason’s group to work on both observational and theoretical projects on galaxy formation and reionization, including analysing data from the SPURS JWST survey. Applicants with interests and potential experience in any of galaxy formation, Lyman-alpha emission, atomic physics and radiative transfer, IGM/CGM evolution, AGN/LRDs, galaxy-dark matter connections, statistical inference, JWST NIRSpec spectroscopy, and comparing simulations to observations are strongly encouraged to apply.

  A third position is available to work with Professor Darach Watson’s group on early universe galaxies and black holes, including Little Red Dots using JWST.

  DAWN/NBI offers creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment, and strongly supports and encourages broad and open collaborations within the department for all prospective PhD fellows.

  Additional PhD positions may be available to work on specific projects at DAWN funded through individual group leadership grants with applications pending in December 2026. Applicants with research interests in any of the above DAWN research themes are strongly encouraged to apply. 

  Applicants to this position will be automatically considered for all available PhD positions at DAWN/NBI at the time of review.

   

  The PhD programme

  Depending on your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelor's degree.

  ********************************************************************************

  Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. physics/astrophysics. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

   

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for a maximum of 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment according to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme 

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor´s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database. 

  Terms of the integrated programme
 To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes in Astrophysics at the Niels Bohr Institute.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see:  www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year.
 A PhD grant portion is currently (2025) DKK 6.820 before tax.
 
 When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme     (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme)

   	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision    	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project    

  We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other relevant professional activities 	
• Curious mind-set with a strong interest in extragalactic astrophysics 	
• Good English language skills    

  ***************************************************************************

  Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Cover letter (max. two pages) concisely outlining your research interests and motivation for applying to the PhD project, relevant research and educational experience. Explain what has shaped your research ambitions, why you wish to pursue a PhD, your relevant past work, and your future career goals.  	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position, any publications, and a list of up to 3 people who could be contacted for references. 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.     

  Application deadline: 

  The deadline for applications is 22 December 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

   

  The further process 
 After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in early to mid February, 2027.

   

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD position, please contact the principal supervisor:

  Dr. Charlotte Mason, charlotte.mason@nbi.ku.dk

  or

  Prof. Darach Watson, darach@nbi.ku.dk

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.
